NASB.1: The Song of Songs, which is Solomon's.
NASB.2: 'May he kiss me with the kisses of his mouth! For your love is better than wine.
NASB.3: 'Your oils have a pleasing fragrance, Your name is [like] purified oil; Therefore the maidens love you.
NASB.4: 'Draw me after you [and] let us run [together]! The king has brought me into his chambers.' 'We will rejoice in you and be glad; We will extol your love more than wine. Rightly do they love you.'
NASB.5: 'I am black but lovely, O daughters of Jerusalem, Like the tents of Kedar, Like the curtains of Solomon.
NASB.6: 'Do not stare at me because I am swarthy, For the sun has burned me. My mother's sons were angry with me; They made me caretaker of the vineyards, [But] I have not taken care of my own vineyard.
NASB.7: 'Tell me, O you whom my soul loves, Where do you pasture [your flock], Where do you make [it] lie down at noon? For why should I be like one who veils herself Beside the flocks of your companions?'
NASB.8: 'If you yourself do not know, Most beautiful among women, Go forth on the trail of the flock And pasture your young goats By the tents of the shepherds.
NASB.9: 'To me, my darling, you are like My mare among the chariots of Pharaoh.
NASB.10: 'Your cheeks are lovely with ornaments, Your neck with strings of beads.'
NASB.11: 'We will make for you ornaments of gold With beads of silver.'
NASB.12: 'While the king was at his table, My perfume gave forth its fragrance.
NASB.13: 'My beloved is to me a pouch of myrrh Which lies all night between my breasts.
NASB.14: 'My beloved is to me a cluster of henna blossoms In the vineyards of Engedi.'
NASB.15: 'How beautiful you are, my darling, How beautiful you are! Your eyes are [like] doves.'
NASB.16: 'How handsome you are, my beloved, [And] so pleasant! Indeed, our couch is luxuriant!
NASB.17: 'The beams of our houses are cedars, Our rafters, cypresses.

NKJV.1: The song of songs, which is Solomon’s.
NKJV.2: Let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth— For your love is better than wine.
NKJV.3: Because of the fragrance of your good ointments, Your name is ointment poured forth; Therefore the virgins love you.
NKJV.4: Draw me away!  We will run after you. The king has brought me into his chambers. We will be glad and rejoice in you. We will remember your love more than wine. Rightly do they love you.
NKJV.5: I am dark, but lovely, O daughters of Jerusalem, Like the tents of Kedar, Like the curtains of Solomon.
NKJV.6: Do not look upon me, because I am dark, Because the sun has tanned me. My mother’s sons were angry with me; They made me the keeper of the vineyards, But my own vineyard I have not kept.
NKJV.7: Tell me, O you whom I love, Where you feed your flock, Where you make it rest at noon. For why should I be as one who veils herself By the flocks of your companions?
NKJV.8: If you do not know, O fairest among women, Follow in the footsteps of the flock, And feed your little goats Beside the shepherds’ tents.
NKJV.9: I have compared you, my love,  To my filly among Pharaoh’s chariots.
NKJV.10: Your cheeks are lovely with ornaments, Your neck with chains of gold.
NKJV.11: We will make you ornaments of gold With studs of silver.
NKJV.12: While the king is at his table, My spikenard sends forth its fragrance.
NKJV.13: A bundle of myrrh is my beloved to me, That lies all night between my breasts.
NKJV.14: My beloved is to me a cluster of henna blooms In the vineyards of En Gedi.
NKJV.15: Behold, you are fair, my love! Behold, you are fair! You have dove’s eyes.
NKJV.16: Behold, you are handsome, my beloved! Yes, pleasant! Also our bed is green.
NKJV.17: The beams of our houses are cedar, And our rafters of fir.

NLT.1: This is Solomon’s song of songs, more wonderful than any other.
NLT.2:
Kiss me and kiss me again,
for your love is sweeter than wine.
NLT.3:
How pleasing is your fragrance;
your name is like the spreading fragrance of scented oils.
No wonder all the young women love you!
NLT.4:
Take me with you; come, let’s run!
The king has brought me into his bedroom. Young Women of Jerusalem
How happy we are for you, O king.
We praise your love even more than wine. Young Woman
How right they are to adore you.
NLT.5:
I am dark but beautiful,
O women of Jerusalem —
dark as the tents of Kedar,
dark as the curtains of Solomon’s tents.
NLT.6:
Don’t stare at me because I am dark —
the sun has darkened my skin.
My brothers were angry with me;
they forced me to care for their vineyards,
so I couldn’t care for myself — my own vineyard.
NLT.7:
Tell me, my love, where are you leading your flock today?
Where will you rest your sheep at noon?
For why should I wander like a prostitute
among your friends and their flocks?
NLT.8:
If you don’t know, O most beautiful woman,
follow the trail of my flock,
and graze your young goats by the shepherds’ tents.
NLT.9:
You are as exciting, my darling,
as a mare among Pharaoh’s stallions.
NLT.10:
How lovely are your cheeks;
your earrings set them afire!
How lovely is your neck,
enhanced by a string of jewels.
NLT.11:
We will make for you earrings of gold
and beads of silver.
NLT.12:
The king is lying on his couch,
enchanted by the fragrance of my perfume.
NLT.13:
My lover is like a sachet of myrrh
lying between my breasts.
NLT.14:
He is like a bouquet of sweet henna blossoms
from the vineyards of En-gedi.
NLT.15:
How beautiful you are, my darling,
how beautiful!
Your eyes are like doves.
NLT.16:
You are so handsome, my love,
pleasing beyond words!
The soft grass is our bed;
NLT.17:
fragrant cedar branches are the beams of our house,
and pleasant smelling firs are the rafters.

AMP.1: The Song of Songs [the best of songs], which is Solomon's.
AMP.2:
(The Shulammite Bride) "May he kiss me with the kisses of his mouth!" [Solomon arrives, she turns to him, saying,]
"For your love is better than wine.
AMP.3:
"The aroma of your oils is fragrant and pleasing;
Your name is perfume poured out;
Therefore the maidens love you.
AMP.4:
"Draw me away with you and let us run together!
Let the king bring me into his chambers."
(The Chorus) "We will rejoice and be glad in you;
We will remember and extol your love more [sweet and fragrant] than wine.
Rightly do they love you."
AMP.5:
(The Shulammite Bride) "I am deeply tanned but lovely,
O daughters of Jerusalem,
[I am dark] like the tents of [the Bedouins of] Kedar,
Like the [beautiful] curtains of Solomon.
AMP.6:
"Do not gaze at me because I am deeply tanned,
[I have worked in] the sun; it has left its mark on me.
My mother's sons were angry with me;
They made me keeper of the vineyards,
But my own vineyard (my complexion) I have not kept."
AMP.7:
"Tell me, O you whom my soul loves,
Where do you pasture your flock,
Where do you make it lie down at noon?
For why should I be like one who is veiled
Beside the flocks of your companions?"
AMP.8:
(The Bridegroom) "If you do not know [where your lover is],
O you fairest among women,
Run along, follow the tracks of the flock,
And pasture your young goats
By the tents of the shepherds.
AMP.9:
"To me, my love, you are like
My [favorite] mare among the chariots of Pharaoh.
AMP.10:
"Your cheeks are lovely with ornaments,
Your neck with strings of jewels."
AMP.11:
(The Chorus) "We will make for you chains and ornaments of gold,
[Studded] with beads of silver."
AMP.12:
(The Shulammite Bride) "While the king was at his table,
My perfume (Solomon) sent forth [his] fragrance [surrounding me].
AMP.13:
"My beloved is to me like a pouch of myrrh
Which lies all night between my breasts.
AMP.14:
"My beloved is to me a cluster of henna flowers
In the [fragrant] vineyards of Engedi."
AMP.15:
(The Bridegroom) "Behold, how beautiful you are, my darling,
Behold, how beautiful you are!
Your eyes are dove's eyes."
AMP.16:
(The Shulammite Bride) "Behold, how fair and handsome you are, my beloved;
And so delightful!
Our arbor is green and luxuriant.
AMP.17:
"The beams of our houses are cedars,
Our rafters and panels are cypresses.

MSG.1: The Song—best of all songs—Solomon's song!
MSG.2:
Kiss me—full on the mouth!
Yes! For your love is better than wine,
MSG.3:
headier than your aromatic oils.
The syllables of your name murmur like a meadow brook.
No wonder everyone loves to say your name!
MSG.4:
Take me away with you! Let's run off together!
An elopement with my King-Lover!
We'll celebrate, we'll sing,
we'll make great music.
Yes! For your love is better than vintage wine.
Everyone loves you—of course! And why not?
MSG.5:
I am weathered but still elegant,
oh, dear sisters in Jerusalem,
Weather-darkened like Kedar desert tents,
time-softened like Solomon's Temple hangings.
MSG.6:
Don't look down on me because I'm dark,
darkened by the sun's harsh rays.
My brothers ridiculed me and sent me to work in the fields.
They made me care for the face of the earth,
but I had no time to care for my own face.
MSG.7:
Tell me where you're working
—I love you so much—
Tell me where you're tending your flocks,
where you let them rest at noontime.
Why should I be the one left out,
outside the orbit of your tender care?
MSG.8:
If you can't find me, loveliest of all women,
it's all right. Stay with your flocks.
Lead your lambs to good pasture.
Stay with your shepherd neighbors.
MSG.9:
You remind me of Pharaoh's
well-groomed and satiny mares.
MSG.10:
Pendant earrings line the elegance of your cheeks;
strands of jewels illumine the curve of your throat.
MSG.11:
I'm making jewelry for you, gold and silver jewelry
that will mark and accent your beauty.
MSG.12:
When my King-Lover lay down beside me,
my fragrance filled the room.
MSG.13:
His head resting between my breasts—
the head of my lover was a sachet of sweet myrrh.
MSG.14:
My beloved is a bouquet of wildflowers
picked just for me from the fields of Engedi.
MSG.15:
Oh, my dear friend! You're so beautiful!
And your eyes so beautiful—like doves!
MSG.16:
And you, my dear lover—you're so handsome!
And the bed we share is like a forest glen.
MSG.17:
We enjoy a canopy of cedars
enclosed by cypresses, fragrant and green.

NET.5: I am dark but lovely, O maidens of Jerusalem, dark like the tents of Qedar, lovely like the tent curtains of Salmah.
NET.6: Do not stare at me because I am dark, for the sun has burned my skin. My brothers were angry with me; they made me the keeper of the vineyards. Alas, my own vineyard I could not keep!
NET.7: Tell me, O you whom my heart loves, where do you pasture your sheep? Where do you rest your sheep during the midday heat? Tell me lest I wander around beside the flocks of your companions!
NET.8: If you do not know, O most beautiful of women, simply follow the tracks of my flock, and pasture your little lambs beside the tents of the shepherds.
NET.9: O my beloved, you are like a mare among Pharaoh’s stallions.
NET.10: Your cheeks are beautiful with ornaments; your neck is lovely with strings of jewels.
NET.11: We will make for you gold ornaments studded with silver.
NET.12: While the king was at his banqueting table, my nard gave forth its fragrance.
NET.13: My beloved is like a fragrant pouch of myrrh spending the night between my breasts.
NET.14: My beloved is like a cluster of henna blossoms in the vineyards of En-Gedi.
NET.15: Oh, how beautiful you are, my beloved! Oh, how beautiful you are! Your eyes are like doves!
NET.16: Oh, how handsome you are, my lover! Oh, how delightful you are! The lush foliage is our canopied bed;
NET.17: the cedars are the beams of our bedroom chamber; the pines are the rafters of our bedroom.
